subject: anaesthesia
title: Total Intravenous Anaesthesia: Target-Controlled Infusion and Context-Sensitive Kinetics

steps.title: Principles of TIVA
steps.tx: **Total intravenous anaesthesia principles** achieve all components of general anaesthesia (hypnosis, amnesia, analgesia, and autonomic stability) exclusively through intravenous infusions without utilizing inhalational volatile vapors or nitrous oxide. Combining intravenous propofol (for hypnotic unconsciousness) with an ultra-short-acting opioid like remifentanil (for potent surgical analgesia) provides rapid smooth induction, pristine intraoperative stability, and rapid clear-headed emergence.

steps.title: Context-Sensitive Half-Time Concept
steps.tx: **Context-sensitive half-time definition** represents the time required for the central plasma drug concentration to decrease by 50 percent after terminating an intravenous infusion of a specific duration (the context). Unlike elimination half-life, which assumes instantaneous bolus clearance, context-sensitive half-time incorporates three-compartment distribution kinetics and peripheral tissue saturation, explaining why drugs with similar terminal half-lives diverge radically during prolonged infusions.

left.title: Context-Sensitive Half-Time
points: Tracks plasma concentration decline after infusions of defined duration
Directly predicts clinical awakening velocity after stopping infusion
Accounts for post-infusion redistribution back into circulation

right.title: Terminal Elimination Half-Life (t1/2 beta)
points: Measures irreversible clearance from the entire body at steady-state
Severely misleads clinicians regarding awakening speed after infusions
Fails to reflect rapid initial redistribution out of plasma

steps.title: Comparative Context-Sensitive Half-Times
steps.tx: **Comparative context-sensitive drug profiles** highlight why remifentanil and propofol dominate TIVA: remifentanil exhibits a flat context-sensitive half-time of 3 to 4 minutes regardless of infusion duration (whether 1 hour or 10 hours) due to rapid blood esterase hydrolysis. Propofol context-sensitive half-time remains under 30 to 40 minutes even after 8 hours, whereas fentanyl rises steeply to over 250 minutes after a few hours of infusion as adipose reservoirs saturate.

rows: Non-specific circulating blood and tissue esterases
High hepatic clearance and pulmonary uptake
Hepatic clearance overwhelmed by tissue storage

steps.title: Target-Controlled Infusion (TCI)
steps.tx: **Target-controlled infusion pharmacokinetic algorithms** use microprocessor-driven syringe pumps programmed with validated population multicompartment models to deliver exact target plasma (Cp) or effect-site (Ce) drug concentrations. The pump continuously calculates distribution and elimination losses across vessel-rich, muscle, and fat compartments, delivering high initial boluses followed by dynamically decelerating infusion rates to maintain rock-solid steady-state concentrations.

nodes.label: Clinician enters patient age, weight, and target Ce (3 mcg/mL)
Microprocessor calculates initial bolus to fill central volume (V1)
Calculates transfer rates between compartments (k12, k21, k13, k31)
Infusion rate throttles continuously to replace eliminated drug

steps.title: Marsh versus Schnider Models
steps.tx: **Pharmacokinetic models for propofol TCI** divide into the Marsh model and the Schnider model: the Marsh model bases compartment volumes strictly on patient total body weight, featuring a larger central compartment volume (V1 of 0.228 L/kg) that delivers a larger initial induction bolus. The Schnider model incorporates age, height, weight, and lean body mass, featuring a fixed central volume (V1 of 4.27 L) with slower age-adjusted boluses ideal for elderly patients.

left.title: Marsh Model Characteristics
points: Calculated strictly from total body weight (V1 = 0.228 L/kg)
Delivers larger initial induction bolus; faster hypnosis
Originally designed for plasma target control (Cp)

right.title: Schnider Model Characteristics
points: Incorporates age, gender, height, weight, and lean body mass
Fixed small central volume (V1 = 4.27 L) with slower induction
Designed specifically for effect-site targeting (Ce) in the brain

steps.title: Effect-Site Equilibration (ke0)
steps.tx: **Effect-site equilibration rate constant (ke0)** describes the delay between drug concentration in the plasma and its clinical hypnotic effect in the brain tissue (the biophase). Effect-site targeting algorithms account for this hysteresis lag: while plasma concentration peaks within seconds of an intravenous bolus, effect-site concentration of propofol peaks at approximately 1.6 to 2.5 minutes, preventing premature overshooting and severe hypotension.

steps.title: Clinical Advantages of TIVA
steps.tx: **Major clinical indications for TIVA** include patients with a proven personal or family history of malignant hyperthermia (since propofol is completely non-triggering), neurosurgical procedures requiring intraoperative neurophysiological somatosensory and motor evoked potential monitoring (which are blunted by volatile vapors), and patients at extreme risk of postoperative nausea and vomiting or undergoing tubal laser airway surgery.

rows: Propofol is completely safe and non-triggering
Volatile agents trigger lethal calcium release
Guaranteed patient safety without ryanodine activation
Propofol preserves spinal cord anterior horn signals
Volatiles abolish motor evoked potentials at >0.5 MAC
Permits continuous spinal cord integrity surveillance
Eliminates flammable nitrous oxide and vapors
High oxygen/vapor mixtures support airway fires
Direct antiemetic action of continuous propofol

steps.title: Accidental Awareness Prevention in TIVA
steps.tx: **Awareness under TIVA safety protocols** demand rigorous vigilance because, unlike inhalational anaesthesia where end-tidal agent concentration is displayed continuously on the monitor, an unrecognized intravenous cannula disconnection, tissue extravasation, or syringe pump line occlusion can cause total cessation of drug delivery without immediate warning. Mandated safeguards include visible dedicated IV access, anti-siphon valves, and continuous depth of anaesthesia (BIS) monitoring.
